title: Linguistic Deception Cues from Forensic Psychology as Cheap Monitor Features

original_idea.body:
# Linguistic Deception Cues from Forensic Psychology as Cheap Monitor Features

**Problem:** CoT monitors rely on an expensive LLM. Cheaper, interpretable deception signals would be valuable as a first-pass screen.

**Direction:** Import statement-analysis features from forensic psychology. Extract them from honest vs sabotage-attempt CoTs in SHADE-Arena, fit a logistic regression, and measure how much of an LLM monitor's accuracy these cheap features recover.

**Why it matters:** Yields an interpretable, near-free CoT-screening layer and tests whether classic deception markers transfer to model deception. Logistic regression, no training.

**Relevant context:** Forensic deception literature; GPT-5 system card; obfuscated CoTs (arXiv:2510.19851).

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain but a gap: cheap linguistic features may recover little signal, and the screening value depends on that.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Feature extraction plus logistic regression; classic beginner ML task.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped: how much of LLM-monitor accuracy cheap features recover.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: No training, interpretable screen; CoT-monitoring tooling labs underweight publicly.

low_compute.reasoning: Feature extraction plus logistic regression, CPU-feasible.

novelty.reasoning: Deception cues studied in humans; transfer to LLM CoT-monitor features plausibly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Deception-cue literature exists; CoT-monitor transfer plausibly open.
